chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn al-Yasa' al-Ash'ari, from his father, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him: Does a man pray while wearing his henna (dyed clothing) if he is in a state of ritual purity? He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.طُورٍ: State of ritual purity (variant of طُهْرٍ)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in henna-dyed clothing?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses a specific fiqh detail regarding the validity of prayer in henna-dyed clothing, affirming that the dye itself does not constitute an impediment as long as the garment is pure. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between ritual purity (taharah) and physical cleanliness, ensuring that common cultural practices like henna application do not inadvertently complicate the conditions of salah.
